entities.name: Liet-Kynes
entities.short_description: planetologist of Arrakis in the Dune universe
entities.description:
had studied him: tall, thin, dressed for the desert in loose robe, stillsuit, and low boots. The man's hood was thrown back, its veil hanging to one side, revealing long sandy hair, a sparse beard. The eyes were that fathomless blue-within-blue under thick brows. Remains of dark stains smudged his eye sockets.

Liet-Kynes (d. 10191 AG), known outside of the Fremen as simply Dr. Kynes, was the son of Pardot Kynes and the father of Chani (who became the concubine of Emperor Paul Atreides). Kynes was the imperial planetologist/ecologist of Arrakis, the Judge of the Change, and the secret leader of the Fremen at the time House Atreides took control of Arrakis in 10191 AG.

Despite his loyalty to the Imperium, Kynes was the secret spiritual leader of the Fremen. Kynes would later become conflicted in his opinion of the Atreides, but found himself allying himself with them. Kynes later aided Paul and Jessica in their escape from the Sardaukar and Harkonnen troops, an action which would cost him his life.

When Liet turned 19, his father Pardot Kynes, the Imperial Planetologist. Kynes was a Fremen child, son of Pardot and a full Fremen Sandrider. Pardot had already nominated Liet to take over his role prior to his death and the transition was painless. Kynes took on his father's mantle and served as both the planetary ecologist of Dune, and leader of the Fremen. He continued his father's vision of gradually terraforming the planet from a harsh desert world into a temperate world with precipitation, greenery, and open water. Compared to his father, Pardot Kynes, who almost entirely focused on the ecologic reformation of Dune and at times appeared to be tactless (though he was kind nonetheless), Liet-Kynes paid more attention to the Fremen and was overall significantly more Fremen and less single-minded than Pardot.

entities.short_description: Desmond Hart in dune.
entities.description:
Bashar Desmond Hart was a soldier with an enigmatic past, who sought to gain Emperor Javicco Corrino's trust at the expense of the Sisterhood. He was later revealed to be the love child of Orry Atreides and Tula Harkonnen.

A charismatic soldier with an enigmatic past who seeks to gain the Emperor’s trust.

Desmond was born on Wallach IX, to Tula Harkonnen, who'd been impregnated by Orry Atreides the night before she killed him. Knowing he had tremendous potential and not wanting him to be exploited for that by Valya, Tula pretended he died and had him swapped with a stillborn infant with Francesca's help.

Little is known about his life after this, but before the series begins he takes twelve tours on Arrakis, a feat since most barely survive their first.

Abu Zide was a legendary figure who was said to have traveled in a frigate which defied the Spacing Guild by riding "there" and back in a day. Used in this way, "there" derives from Fremen mythology, meaning "the land of the ruh-spirit, the alam al-mithal where all limitations are removed.". The Commentaries drew a parallel between Abu Zide and the Kwisatz Haderach, the latter being "one who can be two places simultaneously".

entities.name: Abulurd Rabban
entities.description:
Abulurd Rabban, born as Abulurd Harkonnen II, was the Siridar-Baron Vladimir Harkonnen's youngest demibrother.

The youngest demibrother of Vladimir Harkonnen, Abulurd renounced the Harkonnen surname upon being granted the subdistrict governorship of Rabban-Lankiveil, and through his marriage into the Rabban Family.

Abulurd had numerous sons from his wife and concubines, most notably: Glossu Rabban and Feyd-Rautha Rabban. Feyd was taken in by Vladimir to be his successor at a young age and the elder Glossu went on to succeed Abulurd as Count of Lankiveil following his presumed death by 10191 AG.

Named after his ancestor Abulurd Harkonnen, Abulurd never appears in the novel, but his renunciation of the Harkonnen name in favor of his wife's surname implies that he held distaste for his family's methods, specifically of his grotesque eldest brother Vladimir. Implying he holds some moral strength compared to the rest of his family.

entities.description:
Albert is a member of House Atreides who was the sole survivor of a hunting trip.

Albert was on a hunting trip with his family and Tula Harkonnen. As they prepared supplies, he reminded Ronan that he'd promised to do target practice with Albert. Ronan said they had work to do first. Tula then had Albert help her and showed him how to prepare the animals they were using as bait, taking care to avoid the poison sac that could kill them.

That night, Tula killed the entire family except Albert. When Tula saw Albert, she told him to go, sparing his life.

entities.name: Anirul
entities.description:
For the wife of Shaddam, see Anirul Corrino. Anirul was a thinking machine used by Tula Harkonnen to keep Lila Cho Grace Na-Berto Anirul alive.

After Raquella's death, Valya decided to show Kasha, Francesca, and Tula Anirul, who housed the breeding index. They consulted with her to find the match that would be most advantageous for the Sisterhood. She brought up Javicco Corrino as the father and Natalya Arat as the mother. Valya then had Kasha and Francesca leave so she could show Tula her baby's genetics, which showed that he could shape the trajectory of the world.

Unable to let Lila go, Tula hooked Lila up to Anirul to keep her alive in the storeroom. She had Anirul run diagnostics. When Anirul gave her Lila's vitals, Tula told Anirul to administer spice. Then she further ordered Anirul to keep Lila alive.

When Tula received the blood sample from Valya from Desmond Hart, she gave it to Anirul to run. Tula was shocked when she identified him as being Atreides and Harkonnen and finally identified him as the son of Tula and Orry.

entities.name: Anirul Corrino
entities.description:
Lady Anirul Corrino (d. 10176 AG) was a Bene Gesserit of Hidden Rank who married Shaddam Corrino IV, the 81st Padishah Emperor of the Known Universe. As such, she was the mother of Princess Irulan Corrino and the grandmother of Prince Farad'n Corrino.

Anticipating the imminent arrival of the Kwisatz Haderach, the Sisterhood wanted to open the door for the Atreides/Harkonnen offspring to marry a Corrino daughter and become Emperor. Anirul dutifully complied with her orders and gave birth to five daughters: Irulan, Chalice, Wensicia, Josifa, and Rugi.

Anirul trained Irulan in the Weirding Way and the Prana-bindu methods of the Bene Gesserit.

It was Irulan's opinion that she, her mother and her sisters were adept at avoiding subtle instruments of death.<

Aramsham was a Sardaukar Captain discredited in the Desert War of 10193 AG. Having infiltrated Gurney Halleck's crew of spice smugglers, he and his patrol failed to assassinate Paul Atreides when Paul and Gurney were reunited. He was held captive by Paul and his Fremen, and was later used as an Atreides messenger to House Corrino. He was returned to Salusa Secundus in disgrace for failing his mission, and allowing himself to be captured.

entities.name: Avila
entities.description:
Avila was a Truthsayer and member of the Sisterhood.

While Avila was training on Wallach IX, there was a conflict after Raquella's death because some remained loyal to Dorotea, whom they believed killed herself after Raquella's death, and others who followed Valya. Valya and some of those loyal to her came to those loyal to Dorotea, including Avila, and ordered them to follow Valya or kill themselves as Dorotea had. When they were finished, only Avila remained and she agreed to cover up what had happened there.

Avila came to Valya to review the day's requests from the Great Houses. Valya told her which requests to grant and which to deny.

Avila talked to Tula about the decision to put Lila through the Agony to get information. Tula was resistant, but knew it was Valya's order, so she went through it. They watched as Raquella spoke through Lila and then collapsed, limp and unresponsive.

entities.description:
Baron Yaoufirks was a member of the High Council and the representative of House Yaoufirks.

In order to manipulate the High Council to back investigating Pruwet Richese's death, Valya had the Truthsayers, including that of Yaoufirks, put the idea in their ears. They then decided to invite House Harkonnen to join the High Council, taking Ferdinand Richese's place, and have him make the public call for investigation, which would accuse the Imperium of covering it up. Harrow did this, but then Desmond Hart turned it around, saying that Pruwet had violated the highest law and his death was an execution in service of the Imperium. Desmond then executed several criminals he'd had the guards bring in and Lord Hagal in the same manner.

entities.name: Chani Kynes
entities.description:
For adaption and Canon equivalents, see Chani Kynes (disambiguation)

Chani Kynes [d. 10210 AG], also known by her intimate name Sihaya (meaning desert spring), was a Fremen warrior and Sayyadina as well as the royal concubine of Emperor Paul-Muad'Dib Atreides. As Paul's only lover, she mothered Leto II the Elder, Empress Ghanima Atreides and God Emperor Leto Atreides II.

Chani was born on Arrakis, the daughter of half-Fremen planetologist Liet Kynes and Fremen herbalist Faroula. A formidable fighter by the time of her father's death, Chani served under her uncle and Naib, Stilgar, at their primary residency of Sietch Tabr.

After Arrakis was invaded by Harkonnen and Sardaukar forces, Paul and his mother Jessica managed to escape a Harkonnen ornithopter but found themselves in the deep desert where they were to be left for dead. While sheltering in a large rock formation from a rampaging sandworm, they were intercepted by a band of Fremen travelers including Chani, who were sent by her father to locate the Atreides refugees.

entities.name: Constantine Corrino
entities.description:
Lord Constantine Corrino was the illegitimate son of Emperor Javicco Corrino who was torn between seeking his father's approval and his own happiness.

The illegitimate son of Emperor Corrino, Constantine is torn between seeking his father's approval and indulging his own vices.

As a child, Constantine was with his sister when rebels came in to kidnap her. Constantine knew he couldn't stop them, so he told them to take him as well. Their parents covered this up in order to avoid looking weak and even as an adult, Constantine refused to talk about it.

After Constantine's sister, Ynez, was betrothed to Pruwet Richese, Constantine visited Wallach IX to make arrangements for Ynez to train there with the Sisterhood. He wanted her to have private accommodations, but accepted it when Valya said she would be treated the same as any other student once she arrived. Constantine then returned to Salusa Secondus and told Ynez about the arrangements he had made.

entities.name: Daniel
entities.description:
Daniel was an entity who appeared in the visions of the final incarnation of Duncan Idaho. The character appeared as a homely elderly man alongside his companion Marty. Duncan knew for a Mentat Projection datum that they were strong enough to drive out Honored Matres, and strongly suspected them to be the Ones of Many Faces who had forced the Matres to flee back into the Old Empire. He was also certain through a Projection that they had found another way to use Holtzman's ancient theories. He suspected, although was not sure, that they were independent Face Dancers.

When Duncan Idaho fled Chapterhouse on a no-ship with Reverend Mother Sheeana Brugh, Tleilaxu Master Scytale, Miles Teg, a few Bene Gesserit and a few Jews, Daniel and Marty tried to stop him, attempting to trap the ship in the Net. However, they failed; Daniel knew he saw them but he didn't suspect he saw the Net, and was taken aback by Duncan, who deleted the navigation records of the no-ship in order to escape.

entities.name: Emeline
entities.description:
Sister Emeline was a zealous acolyte descended from a long line of martyrs, who carried fervent religion to her training at the Sisterhood.

Emeline was on Wallach IX, training to be a Truthsayer with the Sisterhood. During one exercise, they examined a brain and had to decide who the man was. Theodosia and Emeline said he must have been a criminal or sociopath, while Jen correctly said he was a survivor. Tula used it to teach them a lesson about the small signs they were learning to detect as Truthsayers.

Another exercise involved them talking to prisoners and determining if they were telling the truth or lying. Emeline listened to hers and said she was lying.

As word spread that Kasha had died, Emeline talked about it with the other acolytes and said that all the founding Sisters were willing to die to follow Raquella's footsteps, though Theodosia believed she was assassinated and suggested they all watch their backs.

entities.name: Evgeny Harkonnen
entities.description:
Evgeny Harkonnen was the uncle of Griffin, Valya and Tula Harkonnen.

Evgeny was living with his family on an isolated planet due to their family being disgraced. His nephew Griffin Harkonnen was trying to improve their family's status. His niece, Valya, disliked how slowly the progress was and encouraged Griffin to find Vorian Atreides and get him to take back his lies about their family, restoring their standing. Griffin tried to do this, but ended up dead, which the family blamed Valya for. They were further angered when Valya persuaded Tula to kill several members of the Atreides family in retaliation.

Years later, Valya returned home for the first time since leaving to commit to the Sisterhood. He said he never thought he'd live to see her return.

Evgeny was distrustful of Valya and told Harrow not to trust her. Despite this, Harrow followed Valya's plans. When they didn't work out how Valya wanted, Evgeny taunted her about this. They argued over the decisions Valya made that led to her leaving their family and joining the sisterhood. When Evgeny began to struggle to breathe, Valya picked up his treatment and kept it out of his reach until he fell to the floor and ultimately died.

entities.name: Ferdinand Richese
entities.description:
Duke Ferdinand Richese was the Duke of House Richese. He was the husband of Orla Richese and father to Shannon and Pruwet Richese.

Under the influence of Kasha Jinjo, Javicco Corrino made a deal with Ferdinand to marry Javicco's daughter, Ynez, and Ferdinand's son, Pruwet, despite Pruwet being only nine years old. As part of the deal, Ferdinand also offered resources to Javicco, resources that Javicco needed.

They planned the wedding and went through with the engagement ceremony. At the party, Pruwet revealed that he had a thinking machine toy, which caused an uproar as the technology was prohibited. Ferdinand defended Pruwet, saying it was just a toy and when Ynez also defended him, Javicco said they could overlook it.

Ferdinand and his family gathered with the Corrinos, except Javicco. Ferdinand was angry that Javicco wasn't there and implied that he would rescind his offer of the fleet of ships. Ferdinand went to Javicco and demanded to see the suspect in Pruwet's killing. Javicco said there wasn't any suspect, so Ferdinand said he'd be taking his fleet back threatened to seize Arrakis.

entities.name: Francesca
entities.description:
Sister Francesca was a strong, intelligent and alluring member of the Bene Gesserit who left a lasting impression in her wake. Once a great love of Emperor Javicco Corrino, her return to the Imperial Opal Palace strained the balance of power in Corrinth City.

Francesca trained as an acolyte alongside Valya Harkonnen and Kasha Jinjo. When Dorotea singled Valya out as being uncommitted, Francesca and Kasha told her that wasn't fair. Then the time came for them to take their vows. They had to stand out in the rain until they were ready to put Sisterhood Above All. Francesca was one of the last to make this vow. When Dorotea and Valya's rivalry caused a division in the sisterhood, with everyone choosing a side, Valya told Francesca and Kasha that Raquella was going to name her the next Mother Superior. However, before she did that, she wanted them both to undergo the Agony test. Dorotea was ready for that, while Valya chose to run away.

After their Mother Superior Raquella, died, Valya said that Raquella had warned them that Tiran-Arafel was coming. Francesca, Tula, and Kasha watched as Valya used The Voice to order Dorotea, Raquella's granddaughter, to kill herself because Dorotea refused to follow Valya's wishes. Valya showed them the breeding index, which determined that Javicco Corrino and Natalya Arat would make the best match to provide offspring to benefit the Sisterhood. Since Natalya was still a child, Francesca was sent to keep Javicco occupied until she was ready to marry him, while Kasha was sent to be Javicco's Truthsayer and most trusted confidante. When Tula gave birth, she decided she couldn't allow her son to be part of Valya's plan, so she and Francesca swapped him with a stillborn infant and told Valya he'd died.

Francesca and Javicco's union later produced a son, Constantine.

entities.name: God Emperor
entities.description:
God Emperor was the title associated with Leto Atreides II after he ascended to the throne of the Atreides Empire. The title reflected both his status as ruler of multiple galaxies, and the formidable prescience he acquired after his transformation into a human-sandworm hybrid.

The title did not endure well after his death. During his life, Leto II's enemies referred to him as The Tyrant, and it was by this title that history better remembered him.

In India, "God Emperor" or "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chakravarti_(Sanskrit_term) Chakravartin]" is a title of a mystical figure which is said to cross the boundaries of several castes, and is therefore able to change the course of history/time. (Chakravartin means "he who turns the wheel of destiny".)

In Egyptian antiquity the pharaohs were seen as incarnations of the god [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horus Horus] (although some speculate that the pharaohs were believed to be gods on earth, descended from Horus). Due to this they were sometimes referred to as ‘god-kings’.

entities.name: Harrow Harkonnen
entities.description:
Baron Harrow Harkonnen was a Baron of House Harkonnen and a rising politician who harbored a strong desire to elevate his House to its former glory.

Harrow attended the engagement party for the wedding between Ynez Corrino and Pruwet Richese. At the party, he made a business proposition to Javicco Corrino, who excused himself to get away from Harrow.

Harrow was surprised when his aunt, Valya, returned home for the first time since joining the Sisterhood. Despite this, he welcomed her in and asked after Tula.

Valya told Harrow of her plan to restore their family name and the Great House's trust in the Sisterhood. In order to be at the palace to saved Javicco from the rebels' plan, she needed Harrow to join the High Council and take her with him as his Truthsayer. In order to get him invited to join the High Council, she had other Truthsayers put in their leaders' ears that they needed someone who had more to gain than to lose by asking formally that they investigate Desmond Hart for the murder of Pruwet Richese. This led to Harrow receiving the invitation. He went to Landsraad with Valya accompanying him, and put in the formal request. When the speaker asked which House he was making the request against, Ynez entered and interrupted, publicly accusing her father. They then watched as Desmond admitted to killing Pruwet, but called it an execution and said it was because Pruwet had a thinking machine, forbidden technology. He then had Horace and Duri brought in and revealed that they were part of a plot to kill Javicco and everyone else in the room via a drone he'd also confiscated. He then publicly executed them plus Lord Hagal.

entities.name: Herald of the Change
entities.description:
The Herald of the Change was an official appointed by the Padishah Emperor Shaddam Corrino IV to oversee the appointment of House Atreides as the steward of Arrakis.

The Herald was sent to Caladan by the Padishah Emperor Shaddam Corrino IV alongside members of the Imperial Court, representatives of the Spacing Guild and a sister of the Bene Gesserit to offer the stewardship of Arrakis to House Atreides. Upon their arrival, the Herald read the decree aloud to Duke Leto Atreides and asked him if he accepted its terms, to which the Duke agreed. He then reminded Leto to place his seal upon the decree with his ducal ring. Once he has done so, he asked the Herald if this has concluded their business and the herald confirms that it had.

entities.name: Horace
entities.description:
Horace came to Division to bring Mikaela the profits from the Arrakis haul, minus what her spice smugglers took off the top. She told him that was expected. When Keiran came in, he showed them that he had been able to scan the whole palace, include the throne room. Horace wanted to use the plans and strike against Javicco soon, while Keiran wanted to wait a bit longer. Mikaela suggested that Keiran's reluctance was him being disloyal to the cause, but he assured them that wasn't the case.

Horace met with Duri, who sold him a drone that could navigate into the throne room and then explode, killing everyone in the room. They then took the drone to show Mikaela. Then Horace programmed in the palace schematics. However, before they could implement this plan, Imperium guards, working on intel from Desmond, who had gotten it from Natalya, arrested him and Duri and brought them to the palace, where Desmond publicly executed them.

She told Piter de Vries that the creature must leave. Piter told her that she could speak without fear, for the creature did not understand their language. She ordered it to get out using the Voice, which compelled it to leave the room.

entities.name: Jen
entities.description:
Sister Jen was a fierce, unpredictable acolyte in training at the Sisterhood School who rarely revealed her emotional core.

Jen was training to be a Truthsayer with the Sisterhood under Valya and Tula Harkonnen. As part of their training, they examined a brain and had to decide what the person was. While Theodosia and Emeline were sure he was a criminal or a sociopath, Jen correctly said he was a survivor. Tula used that to transition to a lesson in the bodily signs they were learning to detect.

During a later lesson, in which they had to determine if the prisoner facing them was telling the truth or lying, Valya challenged Jen, asking why she was there if she thought it was so easy to deceive people. Jen said that her parents sold her to a man who made his money peddling the flesh of children and he killed him and then her parents. Then she admitted she was making it up.

One night, Lila asked Jen why she was there. She knew the story Jen told wasn't truth, but there was some truth behind it. Lila herself had been raised in the Sisterhood and didn't know who her parents were. Jen told her not to worry as the past would find her.

His inept older brother, Hugo Linkam, the previous leader of the House, died in the bullring, and Jesse took up the position before his twentieth birthday.

entities.name: Kasha Jinjo
entities.description:
Reverend Mother Kasha Jinjo was the Truthsayer and confidant of Emperor Javicco Corrino who occupied a position of great influence in the Imperium. A challenge led her to question the intentions of the Bene Gesserit, which left her finding her role increasingly difficult to navigate.

As the Emperor’s own Truthsayer and confidant, Reverend Mother Kasha occupies a position of great influence in the Imperium. When she begins to question the Sisterhood’s intentions, she finds her role increasingly difficult to navigate.

Kasha trained as an acolyte alongside Valya Harkonnen and Francesca. When Dorotea singled Valya out as being uncommitted, Francesca and Kasha told her that wasn't fair. Then the time came for them to take their vows. They had to stand out in the rain until they were ready to put Sisterhood Above All. Kasha was one of the last to make this vow. When Dorotea and Valya's rivalry caused a division in the sisterhood, with everyone choosing a side, Valya told Francesca and Kasha that Raquella was going to name her the next Mother Superior. However, before she did that, she wanted them both to undergo the Agony test. Dorotea was ready for that, while Valya chose to run away.

Kasha was training on Wallach IX when Raquella died. Valya immediately stepped in and seized control of the Sisterhood, influencing Dorotea to kill herself so she could.

entities.name: Keiran Atreides
entities.description:
Keiran Atreides was a Swordmaster who lived in the second century AG. His ambition to live up to his family name was disrupted when he formed an unexpected connection to a member of House Corrino.

As royal swordmaster, Keiran Atreides struggles with the corruption of the court and the legacy of his family name.

Keiran, a swordmaster, trained with the princess Ynez Corrino. He insisted she was improving, though she knew he was just flattering her. He said he knew she'd do well on Wallach IX, where she was going to train with the Sisterhood. When Ynez was betrothed to Pruwet Richese, she decided to enjoy one last night of freedom before her wedding. She met Keiran at a bar and they had sex in a back room.

Following the death of Pruwet Richese, Javicco ordered Desmond Hart be detained and told Keiran to make sure he didn't get out. Keiran did so and then used everyone being distracted by the death to scan the palace, including the throne room, which he handed over to the rebellion, his true alliance. Mikaela doubted his allegiance, but he assured her that he abhorred the way the elites hoarded spice, forcing people to resort to violence just to get what they needed to stay alive.

entities.name: Leto Atreides I
entities.description:
For adaption and Canon equivalents, see Leto Atreides I (disambiguation)

Leto Atreides I (10140 A.G. - March 10191 A.G.) was the 20th and penultimate Duke of House Atreides and the father of Emperor Paul Atreides. Well known for his even-handed and compassionate leadership style, Leto ruled over Caladan and later Arrakis while at war with the Baron Vladimir of House Harkonnen.

A direct descendant of Ancient Greek monarch King Agamemnon, Leto I was famously known as the Red Duke and affectionately called Leto the Just. Celebrated for his fair and compassionate leadership, he managed the reins of Caladan and kept his military well-trained and battle-hardened, despite the softness of their verdant home and utopian lifestyle, as they could not afford weakness with the brutal Harkonnens as enemies.

A model of strong but fair governance over his organized but spiritually content society, Duke Leto became a prominent player in the Landsraad, much to the Padishah Emperor's concern. The fact that Leto's military power began to rival that of the Imperial Sardaukar only strained his goodwill with the Corrino monarch.

entities.name: Leto Atreides II
entities.description:
Leto Atreides II was the third and final ruler of the Atreides Empire and its first and only God Emperor from 10219 A.G. until his assassination in 13728 A.G. — an event that dissolved his multigalactic regime into a tenuous confederation of rival factions.

Leto and his twin sister, Ghanima, were born on Arrakis to Emperor Paul Muad'Dib Atreides and his royal Fremen concubine, Chani Kynes, daughter of renowned planetologist Liet-Kynes. Due to their mother's fatal melange addiction to overcome her infertility, both twins were pre-born — being imbued with centuries of ancestral knowledge in the womb — on top of inheriting their father's oracular powers. Leto II was named after his paternal grandfather and firstborn brother, Duke Leto Atreides and Leto II the Elder, respectively — both of whom were murdered on Arrakis by Harkonnen and Sardaukar forces prior to Muad'Dib's ascension.

Realizing that their pre-born aunt, Alia Atreides — now ruling the Imperium as Regent — had been driven mad by the ego-memory of her late Harkonnen grandfather, Leto and his sister conspired against her murderous regime and its threat to the Golden Path of humanity's survival. However, they were soon separated after surviving an unconventional assassination attempt by House Corrino, resulting in Leto's exile into the deep desert in search of answers to his enigmatic visions.

Following his life-extending bond with a colony of sandtrout and the violent deaths of his father and aunt, Leto II ascended the Golden Lion Throne as God Emperor of the Known Universe and ruled mankind with an iron fist for thirty-five hundred years, thereby guiding it from certain extinction at the cost of his own humanity and happiness.

entities.name: Leto Atreides II the Elder
entities.description:
Leto Atreides II was the first born child of Paul Atreides and his lover (and later concubine) Chani. He was murdered in infancy during a Sardaukar attack on the sietch where he was being hidden.

Leto II the Elder is sometimes also referred to simply as Leto II, and at times Leto II the God Emperor/Tyrant (the twin of Ghanima Atreides) is referred to as Leto III.

Priests on Rakis, some 1500 years after the God Emperor's death, theorized that Leto II the Elder was reincarnated in the second child by Muad'Dib and that a part of him remained in Heaven, nameless, to assist in the transition after death.

entities.name: Lila
entities.description:
Lila Cho Grace Na-Berto Anirul was the youngest acolyte at the Sisterhood School with a deep empathy beyond her years.

Lila was training with the Sisterhood. When she heard Jen tell a lie about her parents selling her to someone who peddled the flesh of children, whom she later killed, along with parents. Lila said she knew that the story was a lie, but also knew there was truth behind it. Lila herself was raised in the Sisterhood and the Reverend Mothers didn't tell her who her parents were.

As word spread that Kasha had died, Lila talked to the other acolytes about it and Theodosia suggested it was an assassination.

Tula then came to Lila and told her for the first time that Raquella was her great-great-grandmother. Then she said Lila could unlock her genetic memory to give them more insight into Raquella's prophecy, giving them guidance on what to do. Lila was reluctant as it would require being poisoned and experiencing Agony, something she hadn't trained for.

entities.name: Maometh
entities.description:
Maometh, the so-called "Third Muhammed", was a Prophet. The Zensunni had originally emerged from a schism among his followers that had broken away from his teachings in 1381 BG.

The name seems to be a variant of the Arabic male name Mohammed or Muhammed or maybe a word-play on it and the Chinese surname "Mao" and the figure of "Baphometh", as his teachings incorporated elements from Arabic religion or Islam, Zen Buddhism and possibly Gnosticism. The name could also be derived from the word "Mahoma", which is the Spanish version of prophet Muhammad's name. entities.name: Marty
entities.description:
Marty was an entity who appeared in the visions of the final incarnation of Duncan Idaho. The character appeared as a homely elderly woman alongside her companion Daniel. Duncan knew for a Mentat Projection datum that they were strong enough to drive out Honored Matres, and strongly suspected them to be the Ones of Many Faces who had forced the Matres to flee back into the Old Empire. He was also certain through a Projection that they had found another way to use Holtzman's ancient theories. He suspected, although was not sure, that they were independent Face Dancers.

When Duncan Idaho fled Chapterhouse on a no-ship with Reverend Mother Sheeana Brugh, Tleilaxu Master Scytale, Miles Teg, a few Bene Gesserit and a few Jews, Daniel and Marty tried to stop him, attempting to trap the ship in the Net. However, they failed; Daniel knew he saw them but he didn't suspect he saw the Net, and was taken aback by Duncan, who deleted the navigation records of the no-ship in order to escape.

entities.name: Mikaela
entities.description:
Mikaela was a strong-willed Fremen woman who serves the royal family while longing for a home planet she’s never known.

Mikaela was working at a bar when she watched Keiran Atreides and Ynez Corrino meet up and go to a back room together.

Mikaela was working again when Horace came in with the proceeds from the Arrakis haul, minus what her spice smugglers took off the top. Keiran then came in and showed them he got scans of the palace, including the throne room. Horace wanted to use the plans to attack right away, while Keiran suggested waiting. This made Mikaela think that Keiran couldn't be trusted.

Mikaela then went to see Valya who congratulated her on the harvest attack. Then Valya asked for the names of everyone involved in the raids on Arrakis. She needed to burn the whole unit to assuage Javicco's fears. Mikaela told her to start with Keiran.

entities.name: Natalya Arat Corrino
entities.description:
Empress Natalya Arat Corrino was a formidable royal who united thousands of worlds in her marriage to Emperor Javicco Corrino.

A formidable royal who united thousands of worlds through her marriage to Emperor Javicco Corrino, Empress Natalya wishes to make her own contribution to the young Imperium.

Natalya helped her daughter, Ynez, get dressed for her engagement party. She was betrothed to Pruwet Richese, who was only nine years old. Natalya didn't approve of the union and told Ynez she wanted her to be able to rule how she wanted and marry how she wanted. Ynez insisted to her mother that she was happy with the arrangement as she could live the next several years until he came of age how she wanted.

Natalya then went to her husband, who said he didn't feel like he had any choice but to move forward with their wedding. Their own marriage was arranged, but Natalya had been the one to broker it herself. But she knew things were different with Ynez and Pruwet. Javicco said that the marriage came with resources they needed, so it needed to go forward.
entities.short_description: Empress Natalya Arat Corrino was a formidable royal who united thousands of worlds in her marriage to Emperor Javicco Corrino.

entities.name: Nazir
entities.description:
Nazir was a member of the Sisterhood and a Suk Doctor.

Following the death of Kasha Jinjo, Nazir came to Wallach IX to examine her body in the hopes of figuring out how she died. Nazir's initial examination was inconclusive and she needed to run more tests, but she was able to say that the heat that burned her skin had come from within her body.

After Raquella, while occupying Lila's body, figured out that it was an airborne retrovirus that had infected Kasha and all the acolytes, Nazir figured out that the virus was feeding off fear, which set off a chain reaction in the body. She decided to expose herself deliberately so she could transmute it and use that to generate a cure. Nazir started the process with Tula watching, but the harder that Nazir tried to fight the virus, the stronger the virus became. Nazir said she couldn't fight it because it wasn't human. Then she started burning and died.

entities.name: Orla Richese
entities.description:
Orla Richese is the wife of Ferdinand Richese and mother of Pruwet Richese.

Orla came to the Corrinos' with her husband, son, and daughter so her son could be married to Princess Ynez Corrino. The engagement ceremony went well, but at the engagement party, Pruwet pulled out a thinking machine toy, startling others as the technology was prohibited. When Ynez defended him, Javicco decided they could overlook it and the party continued.

Orla went with her husband and daughter when they learned Pruwet had been killed. Ferdinand knew there was more to the story than the Corrinos were telling them, but the Corrinos said nothing more about it. When Valya came, she gave them her condolences, but Javicco said that contrary to what they'd heard, there was no suspect in his death. However, later, Javicco had Desmond Hart, who had killed Pruwet, use the same power on Ferdinand to manipulate him into continuing his promised support. Orla begged Javicco to stop him and he did, only to tell them to go home, bury their son, and never tell anyone what had happened.

entities.name: Pardot Kynes
entities.description:
Pardot Kynes [d. 10175 AG] was an Imperial Planetologist who studied Arrakis. He remained there and married a native Fremen woman, with whom he had his only child, Liet Kynes.

Kynes was the first to be sent to study Arrakis, perhaps by Elrood Corrino IX. For Kynes, the planet was an expression of its sun's energy, ready to be reshaped

His opportunity to shape the planet came when he was exploring the landscape in a one-man groundcar behind the Shield Wall, near the village of Windsack, one hot afternoon when he stumbled onto six Harkonnen bravos, shielded and fully armed, bullying 3 Fremen youths. It was a common scene, more slapstick than real, but Kynes realized that the bullies intended to kill the boys; one was down with a severed artery, two of the bravos were down, but it was still four armed men against two.

Kynes triggered his own shield, waded in and had silently had two of the Harkonnens dead with a slip-tip. He dodged a sword thrust, slit the third's throat with a neat entrisseur, and the remaining Harkonnen was felled by the two Fremen youths, as he saved the lad on the ground.

entities.name: Pruwet Richese
entities.description:
Lord Pruwet Richese was the child of Ferdinand and Orla Richese. He was was betrothed to Ynez Corrino.

Pruwet was just nine years old when he was betrothed to Ynez Corrino in a deal their fathers arranged. Pruwet and his family traveled to the Corrinos for the ceremony. At the engagement ceremony, Ynez tried to get to know Pruwet, but he said they didn't need to talk as the ceremony was just a formality.

At the engagement party, Pruwet revealed to Ynez that he had a thinking machine toy in his pocket. When it got free, Natalya Arat Corrino screamed, as the technology was prohibited. After seeing Ynez defend Pruwet, Javicco decided they could overlook it, though Ynez told Pruwet she'd stab him if he pulled anything like that after they were married and demanded he get rid of the toy.

Despite this, Pruwet hid himself away and played with his toy. Desmond Hart found him and told him he had a great power, which he was using to win a war. That required sacrifice and he promised Pruwet's wouldn't be in vain. He then used his power to make Pruwet's skin burn, killing him.

entities.name: Shannon Richese
entities.description:
Shannon Richese is the sister of Pruwet Richese.

Shannon came to the Corrinos' with her parents and mother so her brother could be married to Princess Ynez Corrino. The engagement ceremony went well, but at the engagement party, Pruwet pulled out a thinking machine toy, startling others as the technology was prohibited. When Ynez defended him, Javicco decided they could overlook it and the party continued.

When Shannon learned her brother had been killed, she gathered with her parents and the Corrinos. Then she met up with Constantine and they had sex. She admitted to him that she barely knew Pruwet as their father sent them to different planets, far from each other. Shannon and Constantine both used their union to get information about their families. This is how Shannon learned that Javicco was detaining a suspect in Pruwet's killing, news she relayed to her father, who threatened to withdraw his support in order to try to get Javicco to bring the suspect to him. Javicco told Ferdinand his intel was incorrect and there was no suspect.

entities.name: Theodosia
entities.description:
Sister Theodosia was a talented and ambitious acolyte of the Bene Gesserit who lived in the second century AG. She harbored a dangerous secret about her past.

Theodosia was bred as an experiment by Tlulaxan geneticists and was born with the ability to transform herself into any other person.

Theodosia was training to be a Truthsayer when word spread that the princess Ynez Corrino would be arriving soon to train with them. During their training, Tula showed them a brain and asked who they thought the man had been. Theodosia said he must have been a criminal, but Jen correctly labeled him a survivor. Tula used this to talk about the signs they were learning to spot in people's bodies to know when they were lying. They were all then faced with prisoners and were tasked with determining if they were lying or not. Theodosia determined that her person's words were true, but her intent was to deceive.

When word spread that Kasha had died, Theodosia talked about it with the other acolytes and suggested it was an assassination. She suggested they all keep their guards up. Valya then came to her and said that Theodosia would be coming with her to Salusa Secundus. They made the trip and Valya told her she'd replace Kasha and make herself Ynez's new confidant. Valya took Theodosia to Ynez and introduced them, saying Theodosia would take care of her. Ynez didn't want to get to know her and said she only wanted to know how Kasha died.

entities.name: Tojan Gbangbala
entities.description:
Tojan Gbangbala was a member of the High Council and the representative of House Gbangbala.

In order to manipulate the High Council to back investigating Pruwet Richese's death, Valya had the Truthsayers, including that of Gbangbala, put the idea in their ears. They then decided to invite House Harkonnen to join the High Council, taking Ferdinand Richese's place, and have him make the public call for investigation, which would accuse the Imperium of covering it up. Harrow did this, but then Desmond Hart turned it around, saying that Pruwet had violated the highest law and his death was an execution in service of the Imperium. Desmond then executed several criminals he'd had the guards bring in and Lord Hagal in the same manner.

entities.name: Varota
entities.description:
Varota was a famed baliset maker and artist on the planet Chusuk.

Varota lived during the time of Leto I Atreides, a time where the art of baliset was declining. He was disappointed by the loss of apprentices applying to his studio.

His birth town on Chusuk planned an annual baliset festival in honor of him hoping to spur interest in the baliset again.

In the Dune RPG, "House Varota" was considered one of the Great Houses and the ruling house of Chusuk. The Game also gives the original Varota's full name as "Angostin Varota".

entities.description:
Vera is a Truthsayer who trained with the Sisterhood.

Vera met with Kasha Jinjo, with Vera representing House Richese and Kasha representing House Corrino, to make a deal to exchange resources to secure the engagement of Ynez Corrino to Pruwet Richese. While Ferdinand and Javicco discussed those terms, Vera used her hands to tell Kasha that Ferdinand was targeted Arrakis to sway all the Great Houses. Kasha brushed off her concern, saying the wedding was their focus and they could deal with other issues after that.

When Valya came to see Javicco after Kasha died, she learned that Pruwet Richese had also died in the same way. She walked in on Ferdinand confronting Javicco and signaled to Vera to get the Richeses out of the throne room, which she did.

Valya later privately told Vera she needed to get Ferdinand back under control. Vera said that her counsel had its limits. Valya didn't care and said Ferdinand needed to be brought to heel.

entities.name: Ynez Corrino
entities.description:
Princess Ynez Corrino was an independent young princess dealing with the pressures of her responsibility as heir to the Golden Lion Throne.

An independent young princess dealing with the pressures of being heir to the throne, Ynez plans to study with the Sisterhood.

When Ynez was a child, some rebels came into her bedroom to kidnap her. Constantine knew he couldn't stop them, so he told them to take him as well. Their parents covered this up in order to avoid looking weak, meaning no one outside the palace knew about it. It was the first time Ynez was aware of politics.

Ynez was betrothed to Pruwet Richese, who was only nine years old, to unite their two families, giving Ynez's family the resources they needed. Despite the age gap, Ynez told her mother she was satisfied with the pairing as it gave her time to live her life as she wanted while she waited for him to come of age, including training with the Sisterhood to become a Truthsayer.

entities.description:
Agade Yimari was a member of the Janusian Faithful.

Agade Yimari travelled to Arrakis alongside other nobles including Phaedra Vye, Mon Torsival, Marara Torbin, Priorin Tannat, Len Artuni, Ogdan Barbalescu, Menoria Tamar, Oona Byrn, Venesir Ask, Roella Ramsby, Eulalia Harthorn, Ansel Virro, Bianca Bagetti and Hesperia Farani. Yimari attended a banquet alongside Harthorn, Virro, Yimari, Ramsby, Bagetti and Byrn. She requested that her placement be changed, as she was alergic to a species of planet in the flower arrangement and wished to be as far away from it as possible, which was granted by the butler Theophilus. entities.name: Andrea Ganan
entities.description:
Andrea Ganan was a Mentat in the service of House Atreides.

Andrea Ganan was approached by the Prisoner in Arrakeen. She asked them why Anton Tolliver had not delivered the reports through the usual channels, to which they replied that she would not be seeing Tolliver again. She told them that House Atreides was in a dilemma, for it could not win the War of Assassins while cleaving to its ideals and honor, but to win at the cost of these factors would also be a death to the House. Her solution was to insulate, having certain members carry out the distasteful deeds of spycraft and intrigue without damaging the House's reputation. She informed the Prisoner that Simone Von Konig, her counterpart in House Harkonnen, was also investigating the mysterious deaths sweeping Arrakeen. She tasked them with investigating the involvement of Captain Tighe Skorda and the Sandflies in the outbreak, which she suspected to be manufactured.

Anoushka Hannivar was the proprietress of Hannivar's.

Anoushka Hannivar was born on Lankiveil.

Anoushka Hannivar was approached by the Prisoner in Hannivar's in Harko Village. She explained that three rules were to be followed in the bar. The first was that everyone must stay in their segregated caste area, for the na-familia would invoke kanly if they discovered low-born interlopers. The second rule was that drink prices were non-negotiable and the third rule was that the back room was off-limits. She also told them that the bar had been designed to resemble her homeworld of Lankiveil, with the designs borrowing heavily from the renowned design-mentat, Hansia Einvald.

entities.description:
Ant Nostrum was approached by the Prisoner in Great Plaza in Arrakeen. She told them of the weapons she had on offer and situations in which their uses were ideal. She also explained that there were many pictured of Padishah Emperor Shaddam Corrino IV as both an icon and a metaphor, to symbolise that while he could not be in all places, all places were beneath his gaze. She responded to speculation that the photos contained hidden cameras by stating that the enemies of the Imperium were everywhere and only the Emperor and his Sardaukar stood in opposition. She opined that the Fremen dared to challenge the might of the Imperium and earned their fate, calling them "savage".

entities.description:
Ariadni Athar was the heiress of House Athar.

Ariadni Athar was approached by the Prisoner at The Salusan Bull in Arrakeen. She told them that it was a terrible time and asked them to leave, but they informed her that her house's majordomo had sent them to assist in the matter of a dress. She then asked them to stay and explained that it was more than a matter of pretty fabrics, for her family had worked hard to raise their status and their efforts would suffer great damage if she arrived to the banquet wearing the same dress as Ariste Atreides. She accepted their offer of aid to acquire the dress by any means necessary. She sent them to her tailor to ensure that the dress was delivered in time for the banquet.

entities.name: Ariste Atreides
entities.description:
Ariste 'Ari' Atreides was the precocious daughter of Jessica Atreides and Duke Leto Atreides.

Lady Jessica Atreides obeyed her Bene Gesserit orders and gave birth to a daughter, training her in the ways of the Sisterhood. She named her child Ariste. Ariste received Mentat training from Thufir Hawat and combat training from Duncan Idaho and Gurney Halleck. The Bene Gesserit intended for her to marry Feyd-Rautha Harkonnen, bear a child and seal the bloodline, creating the Kwisatz Haderach for the Sisterhood to control.

At some point, Ariste chose to become a scholar of the Fremen and wrote up a report on them for the Bene Gesserit after Emperor Shaddam ordered their eradication. Ariste was initially interested in marrying Feyd-Rautha, to the point that she declined Zantara's offer to run away with him into the desert. She regretted disappointing him, but chose to pursue the marriage for the sake of ending the War of Assassins between their families. Feyd-Rautha had decided to hold a bullfighting match before they signed the marriage contract, but his brutality during this event (which included presenting the heads of dead slaves to Ariste) led Ariste to call it off. This infuriated Feyd-Rautha, who became obsessed with her and hoped to kidnap her to force her into marrying him.

After witnessing the Prisoner bypassing Sietch Ta'lab's Fremen biometrics, Ariste followed them in and interrogated them to their presence there. She then decided to investigate the sietch with them, where they discovered a message from the Sleeper who revealed he shared the same purpose as the Prisoner. They also discovered an encrypted message, which Ariste realised would be decipherable with an Ixian decoder. The pair were split up when the Maas Kharet interrupted them, but Ariste promised to get in touch soon.

She also informed them of the roles that the Padishah Emperor Elrood Corrino IX and Duke Paulus Atreides played in the Ecazi Revolt, as well as Paulus' death in a bullfight.

entities.name: Brie O'Garee
entities.description:
Brie O'Garee was the daughter of Phin and Tidjii O'Garee and the sister of Phin Jr., Phaedra, Sally and Koda.

Brie O'Garee was born on Arrakis to Phin and Tidjii O'Garee. She had four siblings; Phin Jr., Phaedra, Sally and Koda.

Brie and her family were tracking an off-course freighter in the Hagga Basin when their path was blocked by a rock slide. They were then attacked by the Maas Kharet, who accused them of tresspassing on their territory. They attempted to explain that they were just friendly explorers, but the Maas Kharet called them infidels who were defiling the domain of the electric worms. The Maas Kharet prepared to bury them alive, but fled when a Sandworm approached. The O'Garees reached safety on a rock island and once the worm departed, they followed Koda's signal to the Maas Kharet's camp. The O'Garees killed them, took their helmets and Sally found an old map. They then returned to their shop and prepared the helmets for sale.

The O'Garees followed the the map into the Hagga Basin, where they travelled through relentless sandstorms until they reached a testing station where insects were studied. The family hid when a Harkonnen fire team floated down the shaft from above, realising that they had entered a Harkonnen base instead of a testing station. As they attempted to escape, they encountered a Harkonnen captain, whom Sally and Koda killed in a coordinated attack. Once they returned to Arrakeen, Phin presented their findings to Alastair Christian Chim and the O'Garees were rewarded by House Atreides, as the base had been causing them problems for some time and Gurney Halleck had been planning to lead an assault on it.

entities.name: Drangh
entities.description:
Lieutenant Drangh was a crew member of the Mithra.

Drangh was stationed on the Mithra when it was shot down in Hagga Basin. She survived alongside Chief Hanso and Quartermaster Nasher Hix, but they were left stranded and surrounded by outlaws. Some scouting reports stated the outlaws to be slavers while others reported them as Kirab. The crew's comms unit was hit by a stray bullet, leaving them with no way of calling for rescue.

Drangh was approached by the Prisoner and warned them that she had two marksmen covering her from the rocks, demanding that they identify themself. They told her that they had come to help and she thanked them for their assistance. They explained the situation and the roles of the carriers, the drivers and the Spice Crew. She told them of the damanged comms unit and instructed them to consult Hanso for aid in getting it back online. She then told them that the ship's cargo had been scattered in the crash and that they would need to recover a blue-lattice kyanite crystal, a Torson soundshifter and a twin-polarity microfram, but would need to kill any Kirab who interfered. Once the parts were found, she instructed them to repair the relay beacon they had deployed at a high point in the rocks. However, the distress signal went dead while they were doing this, requiring them to travel through the wreck and activate the comms system's auxiliary power.

Elara Tuek was a smuggler and a contact of Count Hasimir Fenring.

During her childhood, Elara's father would buy her kittens, which he imported from offworld at great expense. However, the environment on Arrakis was inhospitable for the kittens and they always died as a result.

Elara Tuek was approached by the Prisoner in Hannivar's bar in Harko Village. They used a series of hand gestures they were shown by Count Hasimir Fenring to prove that they were trustworthy. She constantly addressed the Prisoner as "kitten", due to her belief that like her childhood pets, they would not last long.

She answered their questions about paying their taxes, warning them that if they did not pay in the allotted time, they would be remanded to a local debtor's prison until the outstanding balance was settled, which would often equate to the death penalty due to a pox.

entities.description:
Marchioness Eulalia Harthorn was a member of the Janusian Faithful.

Eulalia Harthorn travelled to Arrakis alongside other nobles including Phaedra Vye, Mon Torsival, Marara Torbin, Priorin Tannat, Len Artuni, Agade Yimari, Ogdan Barbalescu, Menoria Tamar, Roella Ramsby, Oona Byrn, Venesir Ask, Bianca Bagetti, Hesperia Farani and Ansel Virro. The group were very secretive, refusing to dine with House Atreides, attend the salons or allow anyone outside their group to dine with them.

Harthorn attended a banquet alongside Virro, Yimari, Ramsby, Bagetti and Byrn, during which they all drank poisoned wine. The others died, but she survived the longest due to her toxin modulator. As she was near deathm she was approached by the Prisoner, who questioned her about what had happened. She forbade them from removing her mask, for the masks had been poisoned alongside the wine and sealed to their wearers' faces. She saw it as a fitting end for them due to their tendence to double cross one another. She expressed her dislike of Dhood Shazz and Sub-Prefect Tors, the latter of whom she confirmed had not been present at the banquet. Before she died, she asked the Prisoner to kill all of her servants to prevent them from stealing her belongings and gossiping about her.

entities.description:
Farnoosh was a handmaiden of Morwena Hreg.

Farnoosh claimed to be of Fremen descent. She became a handmaiden to Morwena Hreg, who appreciated her skill with needlepoint. However, when Morwena's daughter Moreg died at her own daughter Nessa's wedding due to exposure to bad Spice, Morwena suspected Fremen involvement. She killed Farnoosh by stoving her skull in with a peppermill.

Morwena was approached by the Prisoner in the Salusan Bull. She told them of Moreg's death and her subsequent murder of Farnoosh.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening

entities.name: Felicity
entities.description:
Felicity was a sietch Fremen who married a town Fremen known as The Vulture. She divided her time between Arrakeen and her sietch. She was killed by Sardaukar while attempting to defend children. Her death broke her husband and he continued to speak to her as if she were alive.

The Vulture was approached by the Prisoner in an abandoned alleyway in Arrakeen. He introduced them to Felicity and apologized for her silence, to which they pointed out that there was nobody there, which he stated hurt Felicity's feelings. He presented a riddle to them on Felicity's behalf and they correctly guessed that the answer was "silence". They asked if Felicity knew what had happened to the Fremen and the Vulture told them how she had died. He admitted that he knew it was insane to continue talking to her, but that he found solace in keeping the one he loved.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening

entities.name: Fiona Thorne
entities.description:
Fiona Thorne was the mother of Aric Thorne.

Fiona Thorne's son Aric was a member of Gurney's Own, an elite strike force that served House Atreides in the War of Assassins. He sent recordings to her in which he spoke of his drive to remain determined despite the visciousness of House Harkonnen. The Atreides had several victories, but many their soldiers died, including Aric's friends. Gurney's Own were deployed to weaken Harkonnen resources on the Easten Shield Wall, with Aric telling his mother that despite their triumphs, he was losing his resolve due to the bloodshed and seeing his own comrades commit despicable acts. Aric was declared missing in action later that month, leaving the devastated Fiona to question the necessity of the conflict.

Redondo Monroe played recordings of Aric's messages and Fiona's diaries on an episode of Through Their Eyes: Firsthand Accounts from the Frontlines, though much of the recordings of Fiona were heavily edited due to her critical comments about the war.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Fiona Thorne was the mother of Aric Thorne.

entities.name: Gina
entities.description:
Gina lived on Amaranth III with her father Rodrigo. The slave Varek took over their villager and placed Gina and Rodrigo in a dungeon. One day, a stranger calling himself the Swordsman fell into the dungeon and they nursed him back to health before using a secret exit to escape. The Swordsman forged a new sword and inspired the villagers to rise in revolt against Varek. Varek was killed and his followers were defeated, though Rodrigo was killed in the conflict. Gina was devastated, though the Swordsman assured her that he did not die in vain and advised her to lead the villagers in remaining steadfast in their duties, confident that the Spacing Guild would return to claim them. Gina thanked the Swordsman and told him she would never forget him, only to discover that he was already gone.

Hester Klimt was the assistant of Osten Laithe.

Hester Klimt was working at the Imperial Planetologist's Office, during which she met Osten Laithe and became his assistant.

Klimt was present at the Salusan Bull after the discovery of Laithe's corpse. She was approached by the Prisoner, who questioned her about her relationship with Laithe and her knowledge of the circumstances of his death. She told them that there was no evidence of foul play and lamented that she now had to deal with the fallout, such as cleaning out his office and preparing for his replacement.

The Prisoner later returned and told Klimt that they believed Laithe had been murdered. She denied this at first, but them admitted that he had become very agitated after meeting with a strange woman. She informed them that he had a secret workshop in the Eastern Shield Wall and provided them with the coordinates of its location. She admitted that due to the absence of Laithe and Cyprian Io, she was essentially the acting Planetologist on Arrakis. She informed them that Laithe had been wracked with guilt and haunted over something he had done. She then expressed her belief that Alastair Christian Chim, Ugo Firenze or Ambrose Lucifera were involved in the murder and revealed that Laithe had recently been obsessed with a revolutionary manifesto and had kept the company of shady individuals.

entities.name: Ilith Richese
entities.description:
Lady Ilith Richese was a member of House Richese.

Ilith Richese was in The Salusan Bull with Orilis Io and Morwena Hreg when she was approached by the Prisoner. Mistaking them for a server, she asked to change her order. They corrected her and she adjusted the ocular acuity of her eye implants. She is appalled that they did not comport themself and they apologised. She assured them that while the nobility were their superiors, they were not their enemies and improved their lives in ways they could not comprehend. She opined that Orilis' grandson Cyprian would be a much better match for Ariste Atreides than Feyd-Rautha Harkonnen.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening

entities.name: Jocasta Cleo
entities.description:
Jocasta Cleo was a sister of the Bene Gesserit.

Jocasta Cleo was approached by the Prisoner in Harko Village. She offered to train them in the ways of the Bene Gesserit. She tells them that she has a task for them in which they must help her research a theory she intended to prove regarding the study of early Fremen bloodlines. She explained that the Bene Gesserit had been studying the Fremen for thousands of years and knew that the Ichwan Bedwine encoded important ancestral data within their holy writings, which she instructed them to locate in the old religious sites.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening

entities.name: Juni Dennick
entities.description:
Juni Dennick was a character in The Graben Gang.

Juni was attempting to listen to her favorite shows on her Communinet Radio, but was unable to due to the noise her parents made as they attempted to mend the water recycler. Her mother Marika suggested that she listen to them outdoors and keep an ear out for wormsign. Her father stated that Sandworm activity had been up 9000% since Zantara took out the Shield Wall, leading Marika to ask how Zantara had done so in one day when it had taken Duv six months to build a shed. He resented being compared to an enemy of the Imperium, which Marika found to be an appealing idea for sexual roleplay, causing Juni to express her disgust at her parents before returning inside.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Juni Dennick was a character in The Graben Gang.

entities.description:
Juno Ezura was a representative of House Lindaren in the Landsraad.

Juno Ezura was approached by the Prisoner to the north of Imperial Testing Station No. 60 in Hagga Basin.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening

entities.name: Justis Clagg
entities.description:
Justis Clagg was a bartender in The Salusan Bull.

Justis Clagg was a Color Sergeant in the service of House Atreides. He lost his legs in the Battle of Arrakeen when they were crushed by a falling Ornithopter and was awarded synthetic legs by Duke Leto Atreides, courtesy of Dr. Wellington Yueh and his cybernetics team. He retired from military service and became a bartender in The Salusan Bull.

Clegg was approached by the Prisoner in The Salusan Bull. He told them of his experience in the Battle of Arrakeen, which lasted 169 hours. He told them of the Harkonnens he killed and his admiration of Duke Leto. They asked him of experiences with bad spice and advised them to go to the upper level and speak with Orilis Io, Morwena Hreg and Ilith Richese.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening

entities.name: Kamelia
entities.description:
Kamelia was a listener of Darko Draganov.

Kamelia wrote to Darko Draganov asking how many times one should report to the Dune Watch network. He suggested that people should submit reports to the network on a daily basis, encouraging his listeners to report any individuals that they found suspicious.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Kamelia was a listener of Darko Draganov.

entities.name: Kara Valk
entities.description:
Kara Valk was a soldier of House Atreides.

Kara Valk was the daughter of a gifted woodworker who was killed by a rejected apprentice. She hunted the killer down and killed him by driving the same weapon he used to kill her father through his eye. However, the apprentice had been the bastard son of a minor Harkonnen noble. The local lord appointed her to his House Guard, altering her enlistment papers to state that she had killed the apprentice before she took her oath. The noble was outraged and demanded a Trial by Combat, in which his Judicial Champion was a 300-pound unwashed behemoth. She and her troop drugged the champion's ale the night before and she made short work of him.

Valk was approached by the Prisoner in the Central Plaza in Arrakeen. She asked for some solari and promised not to send it on semuta, though she then admitted that she probably would.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Kara Valk was a soldier of House Atreides.

entities.name: Katrina Chloros
entities.description:
Katrina Chloros was the captain of the Kytherea.

Katrina Chloros was a soldier in the service of House Atreides. She trained Anton Tolliver, who she found to be sweet and naive. She was the captain of the Kytherea when it crash-landed on Arrakis.

Chloros was approached by the Prisoner in Hagga Rift. Near death, she told them to ask her any questions they wished while they still could. She told them that her family had been loyal to the Atreides for all of recorded time, but they lost their status during the War of Assassins. She revealed that Tighe Skorda had tasked her with smuggling cargo on the Kytherea off the record. They were ambushed over Arrakis and went down alongside the Delphis and the Euphoria. The cargo was stolen by bandits and Chloros believed that Skorda had betrayed them, as he was the only person who knew the significance of the containers. She recalls consoling the rest of the crew as they died and contacting her superiors for help, only to receive none. She received a communication from Andrea Ganan, who advised her to abandon the crew due to fear of infection, but she refused. Chloros told the Prisoner to tell Tolliver that she was sorry before they departed.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Katrina Chloros was the captain of the Kytherea.

entities.name: Kaylen Shiff
entities.description:
Kaylen Shiff was a serving girl who served Lord Petrum.

Kaylen Shiff served Lord Petrum until she killed him, for which she was placed in the slave pens on Giedi Prime.

Shiff was later chosen to compete in the Harkonnen Family Games alongside Amado Delsin, Hollow Tom, an unnamed Fremen, the Grey Lady, Poyko Nen, the Morani Twins and Kanto. They were placed in the Grand Arena, which had been made into a labyrinth. Once the compeition began, she avoided a deadly pitfall trap and took down a cave lurker with a well-aimed shot from her needle gun. She avoided several more traps before she and Nen reached the Abyssal Chamber, where they circled each other over the bottomless pit. She fired at his with her needle gun, but he deflected them with his makeshift shield and retaliated with a swift strike from his dagger. The brutal showdown continued until Nen threw his weight against her and sent her falling into the pit.

Shiff survived the fall and climbed back up the pit. Upon reaching the top, she attacked the Fremen, who moved with almost supernatural speed and impaled her with his crysknife.
entities.short_description: Kaylen Shiff was a serving girl who served Lord Petrum.

entities.name: Kumari
entities.description:
Kumari was approached by the Prisoner in Harko Village. She informed them that she could provide any natural remedies they required to treat their ailments.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Kumari was approached by the Prisoner in Harko Village. She informed them that she could provide any natural remedies they required to treat their ailments.

entities.name: Lena Orlov
entities.description:
Lena Orlov was a character in Death on the Titan.

Lena Orlov was the shift supervisor on the Sand Titan. She was questioned following the suspiscious death of Chief Jarrick Thorne and when asked about the nature of their relationship, she insisted they were just colleagues. When told that Tessa Lim had said they had a close relationship, Orlov denied this, suggesting that Lim was trying to deflect suspiscion from herself. Upon being played a recording which contradicted her claim, Orlov called Lim a "bitch" for recording the conversations of her crewmates. Admitting that she was romantically involved with Thorne, Orlov declared that she had no reason to harm him. Revealing that she had signals training that would allow her to decode the messages that had been sent to Thorne, she was asked what they said.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Lena Orlov was a character in Death on the Titan.

entities.name: Liene
entities.description:
Liene was a guard in the service of House Atreides.

Liene was standing guard outside the Arrakeen governor's palace when she was approached by the Prisoner. She asked them their business and they presented a token, which they said was given to them by Ariste Atreides, who told them that they would help them inside. Liene replied that Ariste had told her to bring them and to make sure that Lady Jessica did not find out. She ordered them to hand over their weapons and clothes, giving them a servant's outfit to allow them to blend in. She then led them into the palace.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening

Luciana was a representative of House Wayku in the Landsraad.

Luciana was approached by the Prisoner in the deep desert.

entities.name: Ludmilla
entities.description:
Ludmilla was a character in Five Days at Carthag.

Ludmilla and her sister were summonded their parents, with their father Hadyn chastising them for addressing their mother as if she were a commoner. As they prepared to leave for the arena, the girls were angry to learn that Feyd-Rautha Harkonnen would not be present, instead travelling to Rossak as part of a hunting party. They no longer wished to go, but Hadyn ordered them to, as he had imported their dresses from Chusuk. He told them that they had no chance with Feyd, whose mate would be chosen for political advantage alone.

There was a knock at the door, which Hadyn to reveal Davros, who announced that he had grim tidings. The girls were dismissed while their parents spoke with Davros. They later departed for the arena in their groundcar. As they travelled through the the backway, Ludmilla complained that she needed to urinate, with Hadyn criticising her for not doing so before they left. An announcement came on the Communinet Radio announcing the death of Argus Veer and a riot that had broken out as a result. The girls were afraid, but their father assured them that their groundcar would protect them. However, Davros informed him that the riot had escalated into a full scale revolt, causing Hadyn to upset the girls by declaring that he hated every member of House Harkonnen.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Ludmilla was a character in Five Days at Carthag.

entities.name: Lyra
entities.description:
Lyra was a character in The Young Guardians.

Lyra was born into poverty and became a skilled sharpshooter. She attended the War Gym at Cala City where she trained to join the House Guard of Duke Leto Atreides alongside her friends Taron and Eamon. They were antagonised by a group of cadets led by Aiden, who constantly insulted them. They were assigned to the Peak of Valor challenge, a two-day endurance test to plant their flag at the summit of Mount Syubi. As they neared the summit, Lyra fell to a ledge below and told Taron and Eamon to leave her behind, but they refused and rescued her. Aiden's group reached the summit first and planted their flag, but despite their loss Lyra and her friends felt pride in doing the right thing.

Lyra and Taron entered the lecture hall the day before their graduation to return a borrowed tome. They discovered a light on in the commandant's office, despite having just seen him on the green. Investigating, they found Aiden stealing the commandant's code book. They informed Eamon, who remembered his older brother telling him of an infiltrator from House Harkonnen in their class. Concluding that Aiden was the infiltrator, they informed the commandant, who had Aiden and his group arrested for espionage and treason during the graduation ceremony. As it was wartime, the commandant invoked kanly and killed Aiden and his group be slashing their throats. He then commended the graduates, declaring them the future of House Atreides. Lyra, Taron and Eamon were then assigned to Arrakis.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Awakening Awakening
entities.short_description: Lyra was a character in The Young Guardians.

entities.name: Mara Bleak
entities.description:
Mara Bleak was a representative of House Kenola in the Landsraad.

Mara Bleak was approached by the Prisoner in a cave close to the Maas Kharet stronghold in Mysa Tarill.

Category:Dune Awakening Awakening Category:House Kenola Awakening
entities.short_description: Mara Bleak was a representative of House Kenola in the Landsraad.
